children: ASX's bear at Macquarie sees signs of life in equities trading volumes at Australia's largest exchange operator. A note from one the investment bank's analysts flags an 8.7% rise in average daily equities volumes as a highlight of ASX's September-quarter result. The average number of trades per day was also up 23% on a year earlier, the analyst adds. However, it's not all positive. Writing before Firmus scrapped its October IPO, the analyst calls attention to weak listings activity and still sees risk that FY 2027 capital and operating expenses could exceed guidance. Macquarie lifts its target price 1.9% to 53.00 Australian dollars and maintains an underperform rating. Shares are down 0.1% at A$60.525. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
